keywords: Swing (transitive) / swing (intransitive) / playground swing lībrō, lībrāre; oscillō, oscillāre lībrō, lībrāre, lībrāvī, lībrātum — cause to swing, sway or brandish something; transitive. Lewis & Short II.B–C includes suspended movement and the swinging or brandishing of implements and weapons. oscillō, oscillāre — swing oneself / swing to and fro; intransitive. Traupman explicitly records this on pp. 53 and 389; Lewis & Short cites Festus. No unverified perfect or supine is supplied. oscillum, oscillī n. — swing apparatus; recorded by Traupman and Morgan–Owens for a playground swing. impellō, impellere, impulī, impulsum — push or set in motion. Oscillum impelle. — Push the swing; our composed prompt for swinging someone on it. Vīsne oscillāre? — Do you want to swing? Virgam lībrā. — Swing / brandish the rod. For gentle back-and-forth movement of a person, Tē hūc illūc movē. remains the descriptive prompt in our Monkey Tree Game.
